audit.whatIsWrong: The entry's central premise is that Blinding Dart shuts off Steel Tempest. It says the blind 'immediately negates Yasuo's Steel Tempest Q autos' (spikes[0]), 'negates Steel Tempest's first Q stack immediately' (whys[0]), and 'his entire Q cycle whiffs into the blind' (wants.you[0]). Blind does not stop Steel Tempest.
audit.why: The League Wiki's Steel Tempest interaction list states plainly: 'Blind: both first target and secondary target do take damage.' Steel Tempest is treated as a basic attack for scaling and on-hit purposes, but it is not a declared basic attack and it lands through Blind. A Teemo who blinds and then stands in 475 units expecting a free window eats the full Q and the third-stack whirlwind knock-up.
audit.corrected: Blind stops his actual basic attacks and the on-hit that rides them; Steel Tempest lands anyway. Spacing outside 475 units is what denies the Q, not the blind.

audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17 seconds. At the level it first appears the real window after he burns it is 25 seconds, not 15 — a ten-second error in the direction that gets a Teemo killed for walking back in too early.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1, 17s at rank 5.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers only ever say Wind Wall blocks your dart. Nothing anywhere says it also blocks the mushroom.
audit.why: Noxious Trap's thrown mushroom is a projectile and the wiki lists it as Projectile-Blocked. A Yasuo who walls a choke does not just cancel your poke — he cancels the shroom you were placing to seal that choke, which is the single most important thing your R does in this matchup.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall eats the mushroom throw as well as the dart — place traps before he walls, or from an angle the wall does not cover.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early claims 'His Windwall does not come online until level 4'.
audit.why: Wind Wall is a basic ability; Yasuo can put the first point in it at level 1 and against a ranged poke lane he usually takes it by level 3. Telling a Teemo he has three or four free levels of unblockable darts sets him up to throw the one dart that matters into a wall.
audit.corrected: Assume Wind Wall exists from level 3 against you, and check for the point rather than assuming a level-4 timer.

audit.why: Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank against a 25-second rank-1 Wind Wall, so a baited wall is roughly three free poke cycles. Sweeping Blade's cooldown is per-target rather than global, which is why 'wait out his E' is not a plan.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall 25s to 17s vs your flat 7s Q; Last Breath 70/50/30s; Sweeping Blade has no meaningful cooldown to wait out.

edits.after: Blinding Dart stops Yasuo's basic attacks but not Steel Tempest — the wiki is explicit that Q lands through Blind, so space outside 475 units.

edits.after: Wind Wall your dart or your mushroom throw — both are projectiles and both die to the wall

edits.before: Level 1 is yours outright: Blinding Shot lands before Yasuo can complete a single Steel Tempest cast and his level-1 kit is just an unreliable skillshot with no mobility yet. Walk up to auto-range only after you see Q fly past or hit a minion, drop a poison stack, then W back before his cooldown resets. His Windwall does not come online until level 4 — throw Blinding Shot freely as a dart and force him to either eat poison or waste a flash. Never stand in the same spot twice; repositioning between Q casts makes you effectively impossible to hit with Steel Tempest level 1-3.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours, but not for the reason most guides give: Blinding Dart stops Yasuo's basic attacks and the on-hit riding them, and it does not stop Steel Tempest — the wiki lists Q as landing through Blind. So the blind is for his walk-up autos, and 475 units of spacing is what answers the Q. Walk to auto-range only after you see Q fly past or hit a minion, drop a poison stack, then W back before it resets. Do not assume Wind Wall is missing until level 4; he can point it at level 1 and usually has it by 3, so check before you spend a dart. Never stand in the same spot twice between his casts.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your control peak: Windwall appears now, so your Blinding Shot dart can be blocked, but Yasuo must commit the wall early — walk toward him to bait it, then circle around the wall's edge and auto-poison from the unwalled angle before his 15-second cooldown expires. Shroom the tribush at level 6 before he can roam for a knockup chain; one mushroom underfoot cancels any Sweeping Blade approach because the slow ruins his minion-hop dash timing. Deny him CS through poke so he reaches Infinity Edge timing without gold advantage.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your control peak. Wind Wall is up now, and it is 25 seconds at rank 1 against your flat 7-second dart — so bait it by walking toward him, then circle the wall's edge and auto-poison from the unwalled angle, and remember it eats your mushroom throw as readily as your dart. Seal the tribush before he can wall the choke, not after. One mushroom underfoot ruins a Sweeping Blade approach because the slow breaks his minion-hop timing. Deny him CS through poke so he reaches Infinity Edge without a gold lead.

notes: The headline finding: Blind does NOT stop Steel Tempest. The League Wiki's Steel Tempest interaction list reads 'Blind: both first target and secondary target do take damage.' The Teemo-vs-Yasuo entry was built on the opposite assumption in four separate places. Second finding: Wind Wall blocks Noxious Trap's thrown mushroom (wiki lists Noxious Trap as Projectile-Blocked), which appears nowhere in either layer. Third: content.mid's '15-second cooldown' for Wind Wall is wrong; it is 25/23/21/19/17. The same Steel Tempest finding applies to Mortal Steel and therefore to the Yone entry.
